start.content: Two men came for my donkey colt this morning. They said "The Lord needs it." I knew exactly what that meant. I've had Zechariah 9:9 on my wall for twenty years. "Your king comes, riding on a donkey." You think I was going to say no?

choices.text: Why did you keep the colt untrained?
The rope was cut, not untied.

set_apart.content: I've had that colt set apart since it was born. Never let anyone ride it. Some things you hold in reserve for the right moment.

rope_question.content: The rope was cut? I didn't cut it — I untied the knot myself and handed the colt to them. Someone else must have cut it after. I wasn't watching the post after they left.

choices.text: You seem very certain about the prophecy.

cloak_reveal.content: I saw those cloaks go by — they used them as a saddle. That's also from the old accounts. When kings are anointed, people give what they have. It's an act of honour.

scroll_reveal.content: That scroll fragment in the tent? It's mine. My grandfather gave it to me. Zechariah 9:9 — we always believed that a day would come when those words walked off the page and into history. I believe today was that day.

choices.text: Tell me about the crowd's reaction.

palm_reveal.content: The palms — that brought tears to my eyes. In the days of the Maccabees, palms meant liberation. Those people understood the language of what was happening.

crowd_reveal.content: The Pharisees' complaint says "the whole world has gone after him." If even they say that — perhaps they're right. Perhaps they just don't know what to do with it.

closing.content: When they said those words, I felt it in my chest. This was the day. I told them: "Take him. Give him whatever he needs." Then I walked down to the road to watch, and I wept. This was not a theft. This was the fulfilment of what I've been waiting for my entire life.
